Our lab is committed to open science. We publicly release the datasets, benchmarks, and code developed through our research. Most resources are hosted on our GitHub organization and Hugging Face organization.

Datasets and Benchmarks

  • YUTO MMS – A comprehensive SLAM benchmark for urban mobile mapping with tilted LiDAR and panoramic camera integration; four sequences totalling 20.1 km (IJRR, 2025). Project page | GitHub
  • YUTO Semantic – A large-scale aerial LiDAR dataset for 3D semantic segmentation: ~738 million points covering 9.46 km² of the York University campus, annotated with nine semantic classes (ISPRS Archives, 2023). GitHub | Hugging Face
  • Q-Drone UWB Benchmark – Benchmark dataset of ultra-wideband radio based UAV positioning (IEEE ITSC, 2020). Benchmark site
  • YUTO Tree5000 – A large-scale airborne LiDAR dataset for single tree detection with 5,000 annotated trees (ICPR Workshops, 2022).
  • Smokestack Plume Images and Plume Identification Masks – Image dataset for industrial plume rise measurement (Federated Research Data Repository, 2026).
  • Unmanned Aerial Image Dataset – UAV imagery ready for 3D reconstruction (Data in Brief, 2019).

Community

  • Deep Learning Reading Club – Our weekly reading group agenda and materials
  • AUSMLab YouTube Channel – Research demos and presentations

The Applied Urban and Space Modeling Laboratory (AUSMLab) at York University is always looking for talented and motivated researchers to join our team. Our research develops embodied spatial intelligence – AI systems that perceive, reason about, and act within physical space – with applications in smart construction, autonomous infrastructure monitoring, autonomous mapping and navigation, urban digital twins, and AI for Earth and space observation.

Open Positions

We are currently recruiting Ph.D. and M.Sc. students (and welcome inquiries from prospective postdoctoral fellows) supported by active research programs, including the NSERC Discovery Grant “Embodied Spatial Intelligence for Autonomous Infrastructure Monitoring” (2026-2031), the NSERC CREATE “Smart Mobility Advanced Research and Training (SMART)” program, and industry-partnered projects with organizations such as Teledyne Optech, Aethon Aerial Solutions, and the Ontario Ministry of Transportation.

Research Topics

  • Neural computer vision and robotic perception
  • Autonomous mapping and navigation (SLAM, mobile mapping, UAVs)
  • 3D urban modelling and digital twins of the built environment
  • Vision-language models for infrastructure and railway monitoring
  • AI for Earth and space observation, including Space Situational Awareness

What We Look For

A strong background in one or more of: computer vision, machine learning and deep learning, robotics, photogrammetry and remote sensing, or geomatics engineering. Solid programming skills (Python, PyTorch) and enthusiasm for working with real-world spatial data are important assets.

How to Apply

Please email Prof. Gunho Sohn at gsohn@yorku.ca with (1) your CV, (2) transcripts, (3) a brief statement of research interests, and (4) representative publications or project work, if available. Use the subject line “Prospective [Ph.D./M.Sc./Postdoc] – Your Name.”

Graduate admission is through the Department of Earth and Space Science and Engineering (ESSE) at the Lassonde School of Engineering. Trainees may also be eligible for the MOVE-affiliated NSERC CREATE SMART training program, which offers enhanced stipends, industry internships, and exchange opportunities.

I am a Professor of Geomatics Engineering at the Lassonde School of Engineering, York University, and Director of the Mobility Innovation Centre (MOVE), which I founded and previously led as its inaugural director. From 2023 to June 2026, I served as Chair of the Department of Earth and Space Science and Engineering. I also direct the Augmented Urban Space Modeling Laboratory (AUSMLab), where we develop innovative solutions to represent, describe, and understand urban environments through visual and spatial data.

My research develops embodied spatial intelligence – AI systems that perceive, reason about, and act within physical space – for smart construction and autonomous infrastructure monitoring. It builds on neural computer vision and robotic perception, autonomous mapping and navigation, and 3D urban modelling and digital twins of the built environment, and extends to AI for Earth and space observation, including space situational awareness. My group has led large-scale collaborative research programs supported by CFI, NSERC CREATE, ORF-RE, OCI, and industry partners, including the 3D Mobile Mapping AI (3DMMAI) project with Teledyne Optech and the KAIA digital twin project with Aethon Aerial Solutions.

I received my B.Sc. and M.Sc. in Astronomy and Space Science from Yonsei University, Korea, and my Ph.D. from University College London, where my dissertation received the best thesis award from the Remote Sensing and Photogrammetry Society in 2004.

Research Interests

  • Neural Computer Vision and Robotic Perception
  • Autonomous Mapping and Navigation
  • 3D Urban Modelling and Digital Twins of the Built Environment
  • Embodied Spatial Intelligence for Smart Construction and Infrastructure Monitoring
  • AI for Earth and Space Observation

Publications

I have published more than 160 research papers. A complete, up-to-date list is available on Google Scholar and on the AUSMLab publications page: https://www.ausmlab.com/publications

Selected recent work includes:

  • YUTO MMS: A comprehensive SLAM dataset for urban mobile mapping with tilted LiDAR and panoramic camera integration — The International Journal of Robotics Research, 2024
  • NSANet: Noise Seeking Attention Network — Remote Sensing, 2024
  • Advancing Physically Informed Autoencoders for DTM Generation — Remote Sensing, 2024
  • CornerRegNet: Building Segmentation from Overhead Imagery Using Oriented Corners in Deep Networks — 2024
  • Fusion-SUNet: Spatial Layout Consistency for 3D Semantic Segmentation — CVPR Workshops, 2023
  • PVL-Cartographer: Panoramic Vision-Aided LiDAR Cartographer-Based SLAM — Remote Sensing, 2023

content.rendered: Dr. Jaewoo Jung published his research work on 3D building modeling methods in the ISPRS Journal (doi.org/10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2019.01.003). This journal suggests an innovative method for automatically updating an existing 3D rooftop model by aligning temporal imagery. The performance evaluation conducted with the ISPRS benchmark data proves the potential of our progressive modeling approach as an effective tool for updating large-scale city models.

Q-Drone is a research-oriented unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), which provides objective path planning to meet the requirements of critical infrastructure mapping such as the complete and homogeneous quality of structure-from-motion results and object waypoint generation for securing a novel view of anomalies. Q-Drone will provide a novel data-driven capability to use ultra-wideband sensors in cooperation with visual sensors (IR and RGB camera) with augmented positioning using deep convolutional neural networks. We provide a unique benchmark for the research communities, called “Q-Drone UWB benchmark”.

Grant Agency: NSERC CREATE – Data Analytics and Visualization; ORF Infrastructure – Advanced Disaster, Emergency, Rapid Response Simulation (ADERSIM)

3D Mobile Mapping Artificial Intelligence (3DMMAI), is supported by the NSERC (Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada) Collaborative Research Development (CRD) program and Teledyne Optech in Toronto. Research grant worth $1,024,000, from NSERC, for this project. Additional cash and in-kind contributions made from Teledyne Optech were also significant: the total cash contribution is approximately about $1.5 million ($1,536,000 total; $512,000 from Teledyne Optech) and $1 million in-kind contribution ($1,048,146). Total funding is $2.5 million over four years. This research project seeks to update Canada’s critical infrastructure – the independent network of utilities, transportation, and facilities. Although Canada is the second-largest country in the world (in terms of area), with the world’s 10th largest economy, one-third of its infrastructure needs a significant update. In collaboration with Teledyne Optech, this project will develop an advanced data processing system using a deep neural network pipeline, which has recently achieved remarkable success in a computer and robotic vision and machine learning. This work will allow for the autonomous recognition of infrastructure assets using high-quality 3D models of critical networks, thus contributing to the field of infrastructure management and improving urban sustainability as a whole.

Overview: Our lab will lead the development of deep learning-based 3D scene classification pipelines including noise filtering, terrain filtering, and semantic segmentation for the point cloud. We will also work on high perception pipelines for LIDAR and visual SLAM and development of the co-alignment network. It will also focus on transmission network modeling.

York University is leading to develop deep learning algorithms for object detection using cameras and LiDAR point clouds.

Our lab will lead the development of deep learning-based perception pipelines which enables detecting rail tracks, wayside objects and moving obstacles using cameras and laser scanning data.

Ontario Train Autonomy Collaboration (OnTRAC)

This project aims to develop the deep convolutional neural networks for supporting the perception models to detect rails paths, obstacles, wayside elements and surrounding environments using camera and lidar scanning data. The developed perception modules will assist in autonomous train navigation and control.

Grant Agency: OCE and AVIN Stream 2
Industrial Partners: Thales Canada and Lumibird

3D Mobile Mapping Artificial Intelligence (3DMMAI)

This $2.6M project funded by Teledyne Optech and the NSERC aims to develop deep learning-based computer vision systems for improving the efficiency and robustness of post-data acquisition process such as object detection, segmentation, environment modelling and utility network modeling with Teledyne Optech’s cutting-edge mobile mapping systems, and a novel SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) system.

Grant Agency: NSERC
Industrial Partner: Teledyne Optech

Layout SLAM

In this project, we study the role of high-level geometric topological cues such as 3D primitive representation of indoor corridors to improve the performance of simultaneous localization and modelling (SLAM) using a low-cost monocular camera. We aim to develop computer vision systems for automatically reconstructing 3D manhattan models to represent an indoor corridor from monocular imagery, and integrate it within SLAM framework.

Grant Agency: ORF Research Excellence – Intelligent Systems for Sustainable Urban Mobility (ISSUM)

Q-Drone

Q-Drone is a research-oriented unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), which provides objective path planning to meet the requirements of critical infrastructure mapping such as the complete and homogeneous quality of structure-from-motion results and object waypoint generation for securing a novel view of anomalies. Q-Drone will provide a novel data-driven capability to use ultra-wideband sensors in cooperation with visual sensors (IR and RGB camera) with augmented positioning using deep convolutional neural networks. We provide a unique benchmark for the research communities, called “Q-Drone UWB benchmark”.

Grant Agency: NSERC CREATE – Data Analytics and Visualization; ORF Infrastructure – Advanced Disaster, Emergency, Rapid Response Simulation (ADERSIM)

3D City Modelling

Dr. Jaewoo Jung published his research work on 3D building modelling methods in the ISPRS Journal (doi.org/10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2019.01.003). This journal suggests an innovative method for automatically updating an existing 3D rooftop model by aligning temporal imagery. This progressive modelling pipeline is developed based on Markov Chain Monte Carlo coupled with simulated annealing. The performance evaluation conducted with the ISPRS benchmark data proves the potential of our progressive modelling approach as an effective tool for updating large-scale city models.
